source.author: lucr
source.text: nam pro sancta deum tranquilla pectora pace quae placidum degunt aevom vitamque serenam, quis regere immensi summam, quis habere profundi indu manu validas potis est moderanter habenas, quis pariter caelos omnis convertere et omnis ignibus aetheriis terras suffire feracis, omnibus inve locis esse omni tempore praesto, nubibus ut tenebras faciat caelique serena concutiat sonitu, tum fulmina mittat et aedis saepe suas disturbet et in deserta recedens saeviat exercens telum, quod saepe nocentes praeterit exanimatque indignos inque merentes?
source.text_original: nam pro sancta deum tranquilla pectora pace / quae placidum degunt aevom vitamque serenam, / quis regere immensi summam, quis habere profundi / indu manu validas potis est moderanter habenas, / quis pariter caelos omnis convertere et omnis / ignibus aetheriis terras suffire feracis, / omnibus inve locis esse omni tempore praesto, / nubibus ut tenebras faciat caelique serena / concutiat sonitu, tum fulmina mittat et aedis / saepe suas disturbet et in deserta recedens / saeviat exercens telum, quod saepe nocentes / praeterit exanimatque indignos inque merentes?
source.text_english: For, in truth, who is able, in peace, to govern with tranquil mind the sacred peace of the gods, who pass their calm age and serene life, who is able to hold in his hand and guide with moderation the strong reins of the boundless deep, who equally to turn all the heavens and to warm all the fruitful lands with heavenly fires, to be present everywhere in all places at all times, so as to make darkness from the clouds and shake the clear sky with a sound, then to hurl thunderbolts and often to shatter his own temples and, withdrawing into deserts, to rage, wielding the weapon that often passes over the guilty and strikes down the undeserving and those who deserve it?

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: quod Lucretius queritur, cum dicit de deo: tum fulmina mittat et aedis ipse suas disturbet et in deserta recedens saeuiat exercens telum, quod saepe nocentes praeterit exanimatque indignos inque merentes.
reuse.text_original: quod Lucretius queritur, cum dicit de deo: tum fulmina mittat et aedis ipse suas disturbet et in deserta recedens saeuiat exercens telum, quod saepe nocentes praeterit exanimatque indignos inque merentes.
reuse.text_english: which Lucretius complains of, when he says of God: then let him hurl thunderbolts and himself destroy his own temples and, withdrawing into deserts, rage, wielding a weapon that often passes over the guilty and strikes down the undeserving, even the innocent.
